Empirical Research Plan                                         

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Method: Staggered Difference-in-Differences (DiD) complemented by an event-study.  
Rationale:
•  The year in which a Specific Trade Concern (STC) is first raised against an importing country–HS4 pair constitutes a well-dated, plausibly exogenous shock to the stringency/uncertainty of SPS regulation.  
•  We observe many product–destination cells that never receive a concern, or receive it later, furnishing a natural comparison group.  
•  The panel (1996-2005) allows multiple pre- and post-treatment periods, letting us test the parallel-trends assumption and study dynamics.  
•  Firm-size heterogeneity can be added through interactions, yielding triple-difference estimates.  
•  Recent advances (Sun & Abraham 2021; Callaway & Sant’Anna 2021) eliminate bias from staggered timing, so we will use those estimators.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Unit of observation: firm i – product p (HS4) – destination d – year t.

Treatment variable
T_pdt  = 1 if importer d faced its first SPS concern on product p in year τ ≤ t
          AND the concern is not yet resolved in t
        = 0 otherwise.

•  “First raised” year τ is the treatment start; treatment persists until the concern is reported “resolved” (or until sample end if unresolved).  
•  Alternative (robustness): drop post-resolution years or code them as 0.

Control group
All firm-product-destination-year observations where:
•  No STC has been raised on that product-destination yet in t, and  
•  The product-destination may receive a concern later (not dropped, but coded 0 until τ).

Treatment timing
Event time k = t – τ with k = …–3, –2, –1, 0, 1, 2, … ; we omit k = –1 to normalize pre-trends.  
Staggered timing handled with interaction-weighted (IW) or doubly-robust ATT estimators.

No RDD is planned, so no running variable.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of a concern, treated and not-yet-treated product–destination pairs would have continued to evolve similarly.  
Plausibility: Concerns are often triggered by scientific or political events unrelated to French exporters; we will show pre-treatment trends are flat.

A2. No anticipation: Firms do not systematically adjust exports before the concern is officially raised.  
Plausibility: STCs are often tabled soon after the importing country publishes or enforces the regulation; advance information leakages to French firms are unlikely but testable via pre-event leads.

A3. Stable treatment: Once a concern is raised, its intensity is similar across firms within the same p-d cell.  
Plausibility: The regulation applies to all exporters; we allow heterogeneity only by firm size.

A4. SUTVA: A concern on (p,d) does not directly affect exports of product p to other destinations or other products to destination d.  
Plausibility: Some spillovers (re-routing exports) are possible. We will conduct placebo tests on (p, other d) and (other p, d).

A5. Exogenous timing of resolution (for specifications that treat resolution as “treatment off”).  
Plausibility: Resolutions are typically negotiated by governments, less likely tied to a particular French firm’s outcomes; we will re-estimate dropping the post-resolution years.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Threat 1: Endogenous concerns – STCs may be filed because French exports in that market were already rising (reverse causality).  
•  Mitigation: Event-study pre-trends; importer-product fixed effects absorb level differences; include contemporaneous changes in applied tariffs and GDP_d,t.

Threat 2: Confounding shocks – e.g., disease outbreaks (BSE, avian flu) that both trigger SPS measures and hurt demand.  
•  Mitigation: Importer-year × product-section fixed effects; remove diseases explicitly documented in OIE database; robustness drop food-safety animal products.

Threat 3: Two-way FE bias under staggered adoption.  
•  Mitigation: Use Sun-Abraham “sa” estimator (package fixest::sunab) and Callaway-Sant’Anna group-specific ATT; report both.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
#############################################
# 0. Packages
#############################################
library(data.table)     # fast data handling
library(fixest)         # Sun-Abraham DiD
library(CSdid)          # Callaway-Sant’Anna
library(ggplot2)

#############################################
# 1. Load Data (CSV placeholders)
#############################################
cust <- fread("fr_customs_1995_2005.csv")      # firm, year, dest, hs8, value, qty
stc  <- fread("wto_stc_1995_2011.csv")         # dest, hs4, year_raised, year_resolved
tar  <- fread("trains_tariffs.csv")            # dest, hs4, year, tariff

#############################################
# 2. Prepare Panel at firm-HS4-dest-year
#############################################
# Collapse hs8 to hs4 & keep extra-EU etc.
cust[, hs4 := substr(hs8,1,4)]
cust <- cust[dest %chin% extra_EU_list]

# Construct outcomes
cust[, ln_value := log(value)]
cust[, exporter_active := 1]                              # presence indicator

#############################################
# 3. Merge Treatment
#############################################
# Build product-dest-year treatment status
stc[, ':='(t_start = year_raised,
           t_end   = fifelse(is.na(year_resolved), 9999, year_resolved))]

# Expand to year level (1996-2005)
stc_exp <- stc[, .(year = 1996:2005), by = .(dest, hs4, t_start, t_end)]
stc_exp[, treated := year >= t_start & year < t_end]

# Merge
setkeyv(cust, c("dest","hs4","year"))
setkeyv(stc_exp, c("dest","hs4","year"))
panel <- stc_exp[cust, nomatch=0]           # inner join

#############################################
# 4. Firm Size Categories
#############################################
# Compute pre-treatment average exports to define size terciles
size <- panel[year < 1996, 
              .(pre_exp = sum(value)), by = firm]
size[, size_cat := cut(pre_exp,
                       breaks = quantile(pre_exp, probs=c(0,1/3,2/3,1)),
                       labels = c("Small","Medium","Large"),
                       include.lowest=TRUE)]
panel <- merge(panel, size[,.(firm,size_cat)], by="firm")

#############################################
# 5. Sun-Abraham Main Regression
#############################################
# Event-time indicator
panel[, g := ifelse(treated==1 & year==t_start, year, NA)]   # cohort

est <- feols(exporter_active ~ sunab(g, year) |
                           firm + dest*hs4 + year, 
             data = panel, cluster = ~dest*hs4)

etable(est, type="text")

#############################################
# 6. Heterogeneity by Firm Size (triple-diff)
#############################################
est_size <- feols(exporter_active ~ sunab(g,year)*size_cat |
                               firm + dest*hs4 + year,
                  data = panel, cluster = ~dest*hs4)
etable(est_size, type="text")

#############################################
# 7. Callaway-Sant’Anna ATT as Robustness
#############################################
cs <- att_gt(yname="exporter_active",
             gname="t_start",
             idname="firm",
             tname="year",
             xformla = NULL,
             data = panel,
             control_group = "notyettreated")
agg_effects <- aggte(cs, type="dynamic")
summary(agg_effects)

#############################################
# 8. Additional Robustness: Drop Post-Resolution Years
#############################################
panel2 <- panel[year < t_end]
est2 <- feols(exporter_active ~ sunab(g,year) |
                            firm + dest*hs4 + year,
              data = panel2, cluster = ~dest*hs4)
etable(est, est2, type="text")
```

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Theory: Stricter SPS rules raise fixed compliance costs.  
Predictions (treated vs control):
•  Entry probability ↓ (5-7 pp on a baseline of ~30 %).  
•  Conditional export value ↓ (~10 %).  
•  Export prices ↑ (compliance costs partially passed through; 2-4 %).  
Heterogeneity: Small firms (lower scale to spread fixed costs) experience larger negative extensive-margin effects; large firms may partly offset through higher prices.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1: Parallel pre-treatment trends confirmed by event-study ………………… 1  
C2: No anticipation (flat leads) ……………………………………………………… 1  
C3: Treatment exogeneity (concerns not driven by French firms) …………… 0.5  
C4: No spillovers across products/destinations …………………………………… 0.5  
C5: Proper estimator for staggered timing (SA / CS) …………………………… 1  

Total (out of 5) ........................................................................ 4.0
